external_entities.description: Other teams' backends that call the inference gateway.

external_entities.notes: Keys are issued per calling team and have never been expired.

external_entities.name: ML engineers
external_entities.description: People who publish new model artifacts to the registry bucket.
external_entities.source_excerpt: ML engineers publish new model artifacts to the registry bucket
external_entities.notes: I'm not sure what governs who can push — I think it is a shared group account.

processes.name: inference gateway
processes.description: A FastAPI service on GKE that receives inference requests and forwards them to the model server.
processes.source_excerpt: our inference gateway, a FastAPI service on GKE

processes.name: model server
processes.description: The service that runs the actual model on GPU nodes and reads model artifacts and customer features.
processes.source_excerpt: the model server, which runs the actual model on GPU nodes in our model network

data_stores.name: model registry bucket
data_stores.description: A bucket from which the model server loads model artifacts at startup.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The model server loads model artifacts from a model registry bucket at startup
data_stores.notes: I don't believe anything verifies the artifact hasn't been swapped — we just trust the bucket.

data_stores.name: Redis feature store
data_stores.description: A Redis store containing customer features such as account age and spend bands per customer.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The features include account age and spend bands per customer.
data_stores.notes: Redis has no password on it; it is only reachable inside the model network.

data_stores.name: inference log
data_stores.description: A BigQuery log containing every request and response for debugging, including raw prompts.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The gateway writes every request and response into an inference log in BigQuery
data_stores.notes: That means raw prompts, which sometimes carry whatever the calling team's users typed.

data_flows.name: call inference
data_flows.description: Calling services send inference requests to the inference gateway.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Other teams' backends call our inference gateway
data_flows.notes: Callers pass an API key in a header. Keys are issued per calling team and we have never expired one.

data_flows.name: forward request
data_flows.description: The inference gateway forwards inference requests to the model server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The gateway forwards the request to the model server

data_flows.name: load artifacts
data_flows.description: The model server loads model artifacts from the model registry bucket at startup.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The model server loads model artifacts from a model registry bucket at startup
data_flows.notes: It uses its own service account for that. I don't believe anything verifies the artifact hasn't been swapped — we just trust the bucket.

data_flows.name: read features
data_flows.description: The model server reads customer features from the Redis feature store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Requests often need customer features, which the model server reads from a Redis feature store on the same network.
data_flows.notes: Redis has no password on it; it is only reachable inside the model network.
data_flows.data_description: customer features, including account age and spend bands per customer

data_flows.name: write inference log
data_flows.description: The gateway writes every request and response to the inference log for debugging.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The gateway writes every request and response into an inference log in BigQuery, for debugging.
data_flows.notes: The logged requests include raw prompts, which sometimes carry whatever the calling team's users typed.

data_flows.description: ML engineers publish new model artifacts to the model registry bucket.

data_flows.notes: I'm not sure what governs who can push — I think it is a shared group account.
